title: "FAQ: what Stokastisk is and is not"
description: "Answers about Stokastisk: an independent open-source Python SDK for vLLM on Kaggle dual Tesla T4 GPUs; relation to vLLM and other projects, supported hardware, models and licence."
guide-section: "Design"
---

## What is Stokastisk?

An independent, open-source Python 3.13 SDK for **Kaggle's dual NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPUs**. It bundles vLLM 0.25.1 built for SM75 (compute capability 7.5) with CUDA 13.0 and runs attention only through vLLM's Triton backend (`TRITON_ATTN`). It adds a validated configuration, a safe `LLM` lifecycle, structured output, an OpenAI-compatible server wrapper, tensor, pipeline and replica parallelism, topology discovery and diagnostics.

## Is it related to the "Stochastic" AI organisation or to the vLLM project?

No. "Stokastisk" is the name of this independent SDK and is not affiliated with any company named Stochastic. vLLM is a separate Apache-2.0 project; Stokastisk bundles a modified copy of vLLM 0.25.1 (Flash-family modules removed) and is not endorsed by the vLLM project or by NVIDIA or Kaggle. "NVIDIA" and "Tesla T4" name the hardware the SDK targets.

## Why does it exist?

Kaggle's T4s are compute capability 7.5. This SDK ships a vLLM tree in which only the Triton attention backend can be selected, and verifies that choice at runtime (`llm.verify_attention_backend()`).

## Which hardware and software are supported?

Kaggle notebooks with 2 × Tesla T4, Python 3.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0 and CUDA 13.0, FP16. Not supported: bfloat16, FlashAttention, FlashInfer, FlashMLA, native FP8/FP4, L4/SM89, Mistral-family models, OpenTelemetry exporters, and calling `vllm.LLM` or `vllm serve` directly.

## Which models work?

Exactly three checkpoints were run on Kaggle: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, in the modes listed under [Diagnostics](diagnostics-compatibility.qmd#the-verified-models). Anything else reports `UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_EVIDENCE`: unproven, not forbidden.

## Is two GPUs faster than one?

Not for a model that fits one T4. The GPUs share a PCIe host bridge (no NVLink), and TP=2, PP=2 and replicas were slower than TP=1 in the recorded runs. Use two GPUs when the model does not fit one.

## Is it on PyPI?

No. It installs from a wheel on Hugging Face; see [Install](installation.qmd).

## Which licence?

Apache-2.0. vLLM is Apache-2.0, copyright the vLLM project.

## Where are the source, wheels and issues?

Source and issues: [github.com/stokastisk-ai/stokastisk](https://github.com/stokastisk-ai/stokastisk). Wheels: [huggingface.co/waqasm86/stokastisk](https://huggingface.co/waqasm86/stokastisk). Release: [v0.1.0](https://github.com/stokastisk-ai/stokastisk/releases/tag/v0.1.0).
